blocks.x: The law governing the **powers, procedures and control** of administrative authorities — it grows wherever the state acts on the citizen.
blocks.th: **Dicey** initially denied its existence in England; **droit administratif** in France showed otherwise.
blocks.in: Expansion of the welfare and regulatory state made it unavoidable.
blocks.gl: French Conseil d'État as a separate administrative jurisdiction.
blocks.w: Administrative law is the price of the **administrative state**.

blocks.x: **Supremacy of law, equality before law, and rights derived from ordinary law** — Dicey's three meanings.
blocks.th: **A.V. Dicey**; criticised for ignoring necessary discretion and for misreading droit administratif.
blocks.in: Article 14; judicial review as basic structure; *Kesavananda*'s rule-of-law element.
blocks.w: Modern rule of law accommodates **discretion bounded by criteria and reasons**.

blocks.x: Rule-making by the executive under a parent Act — necessary in a technical state, dangerous without limits.
blocks.th: **Delhi Laws Act (1951)** — **essential legislative functions cannot be delegated**; the legislature must lay down policy and standard.
blocks.in: Volume of rules far exceeds primary legislation; the **Committee on Subordinate Legislation** scrutinises a fraction.
blocks.gl: Henry VIII clauses in the UK.
blocks.w: The gap is not delegation but **scrutiny capacity**.

blocks.x: Unavoidable because rules cannot foresee every case; dangerous because it is where arbitrariness enters.
blocks.in: Licensing, transfers, sanction of prosecution, discretionary quotas.
blocks.w: The remedy is not abolition but **criteria stated in advance, reasons recorded, and review**.

blocks.x: **Nemo judex in causa sua** and **audi alteram partem**, with the modern addition of a **reasoned order**.
blocks.th: **A.K. Kraipak (1969)** blurred the quasi-judicial/administrative line; **Maneka (1978)** made audi alteram partem implicit in Article 21.
blocks.in: Departmental inquiries under Article 311; show-cause notices; blacklisting.
blocks.w: Natural justice now attaches to **administrative action affecting rights**, not just quasi-judicial acts.

blocks.x: Tribunals decide disputes with speed, expertise and low cost, at the price of uniform procedure and independence.
blocks.th: **Articles 323A and 323B** (42nd Amendment); *L. Chandra Kumar* (1997) preserved High Court review as basic structure.
blocks.in: CAT, NCLT, NGT, TDSAT; *Rojer Mathew* struck down executive control over appointments and tenure; **National Tribunals Commission** repeatedly directed and never created.
blocks.gl: UK tribunals service after the Leggatt review.
blocks.w: India's settlement: tribunals as **courts of first instance with High Court review preserved**.

blocks.x: Legal instruments against maladministration: **PC Act 1988 (amended 2018)**, PMLA, Benami, FEO Act.
blocks.in: **Section 17A prior approval** before enquiry into an official decision; Section 19 sanction extended to retired officials.
blocks.w: The 2018 amendment protects **decision-makers**; whether it also protects **corruption** is the debate.

blocks.x: An independent officer investigating maladministration on citizen complaint, working by report and publicity.
blocks.th: Swedish origin, 1809; First ARC proposed Lokpal and Lokayukta.
blocks.in: Lokpal (2019), state Lokayuktas, CPGRAMS with a 13-day average and an independent feedback unit; the **Grievance Redress Bill of 2011 never enacted**.
blocks.w: India built the **anti-corruption** ombudsman and skipped the **grievance** statute.
